name: Washington

law.name: Uniform Athlete Agents Act with RUAAA terms (RCW 19.225)

covers_nil_agents: Yes. The act covers agents for endorsement contracts (RCW 19.225.010). It does not use the words name, image or likeness.
contract_warning: Warning to student athlete. If you sign this contract: (a) you may lose your eligibility to compete as a student athlete in your sport; (b) both you and your athlete agent must notify your athletic director, if you have an athletic director, at least seventy-two hours prior to entering into an agency contract that you intend to enter into this contract and provide the name and contact information of the athlete agent and again within seventy-two hours after entering into an agency contract that you have entered into this contract and provide the name and contact information of the athlete agent; and (c) you may cancel this contract within 14 days after signing it. Cancellation of this contract may not reinstate your eligibility as a student athlete in your sport.
summary: No state license. Give each athlete a sworn disclosure form the day you first contact them. Tell the athletic director 72 hours before and after signing.

steps.detail: Washington has no registration. You give a disclosure form to each athlete instead.

steps.text: Fill out the athlete agent disclosure form once
steps.detail: Signed under penalty of perjury. Jobs, training, athletes, owners and any legal history. You can use another state's registration papers plus a list of changes instead.

steps.text: Register with each school's compliance office, if it asks
steps.detail: Most schools have their own agent sign-up.

steps.text: Tell the athletic director in writing before you first contact the athlete
steps.detail: This includes reaching out through someone else. If the athlete reached out first, tell the athletic director within 10 days.

steps.text: Use a signed, written contract with all required items
steps.detail: Your pay and how it's figured, anyone else being paid, expenses, services, length and date signed.

steps.text: Put the warning to student athlete in the contract in bold
steps.detail: Use the state's wording. It must be easy to see.

steps.text: Have the athlete sign a separate eligibility warning
steps.detail: A parent or guardian signs too if the athlete is a minor.

steps.text: Give the athlete a copy of the contract and the signed warning when they sign
Tell the athletic director in writing at least 72 hours before signing
steps.detail: Washington wants notice before and after signing. The athlete must tell the athletic director too.

steps.text: Tell the athletic director again within 72 hours after signing
steps.detail: Or before the athlete's next game, if that comes first.

steps.text: Let the athlete cancel within 14 days of signing
steps.detail: They don't owe you anything if they cancel. They can't give up this right.

steps.text: If the athlete enrolls at a school later, tell its athletic director within 72 hours
steps.detail: If you knew the athlete before they enrolled and they get an athletic scholarship, tell the school within 10 days of enrolling.

steps.text: Date the contract the day it's signed
steps.detail: State law and federal law (SPARTA) ban pre-dating or post-dating it.

steps.text: Give each athlete the disclosure form on day one
steps.detail: If the athlete contacted you first, within 7 days. You can't sign a contract until you give it.
Names and addresses, contracts and recruiting costs. A court can order you to hand them over.

steps.text: Don't give gifts that could cost the athlete eligibility
steps.detail: If you do, tell the athletic director within 72 hours. The athlete must also sign a note saying they know the risk.

steps.text: Never lie or make false promises to get an athlete to sign
steps.detail: Never ask an athlete to give up their rights under this law. Breaking these rules can be a felony.

watch_list.item: Federal Protect College Sports Act of 2026 (S.4668)
watch_list.status: Passed the Senate on Sept 28, 2026. The House is out until Nov 9 and leaders say it won't pass as-is. It dies if not enacted by Jan 3, 2027.
watch_list.impact: It would require every NIL agent to register in a state, cap agent fees at 5% of an endorsement deal and limit contracts to the athlete's eligibility.
